page.layout: One column of running text with italic question headings set apart; no marginal notes. Printed page 460 at the head, running head "DE RUDIMENTIS" at the top centre.

main_text.l: alicujus, quia tunc ei, cujus eft, licet pifcari, & non a-
liis, Nam Ulpianus inquit: In laçu, qui mei domini
eft, utique pifcari aliquem prohibere poffum. l. inju-
riarum in fine. ff. de injuriis & famof. libell.
Quæ in civitatibus funt,
Theatra, ftadia & fiqua
alia lunt civitatum communia. §. univerfitatis. inft. cod.
Nullius funt res facræ & religiofæ, & fanctæ: quod
enim Divini juris eft, id nullius in bonis eft. §. nul-
lius. inft. cod.
Sacræ res funt quæ ritè per pontifices Deo confe-
cratæ funt: veluti ædes facræ, & donaria, quæ ritè ad
minifterium Dei dedicata funt: quæ etiam alienari
& obligari prohibuit Imperator, excepta caufa re-
demptionis captivorum. §. facræ res. inft. cod.
Religiofum locum unufquifque fua voluntate fa-
cit, dum mortuum infert in locum fuum. §. religio-
fum. inft. cod.
Sanctæ
res veluti muri & portæ civitatis, quodam-
modo Divini juris funt: & ideo nullius in bonis funt.
Ideo autem muros sanctos dicimus, quia pœna ca-
pitis constituta est in eos, qui aliquid in muros deli-
querint. §. sanctæ quoq; inst. cod.
Singulorum hominum multis modis res fiunt:
quarundam enim rerum dominiū nancifcimur jure
naturali, quod ficut diximus appellatur jus gentiū:
quarundam verò jure civili. §. singulorum. inst. cod.
Dominium est jus de re corporali perfectè
dispo-nendi

page.notes: A dark ink stain lies beside the line "quoq; inst. cod." and is not text, so it is left out. The "s" in the printed "fanctæ" and "fanctos" is a long s; it is written as a plain s. Some headings are set in italic with the word "Dominium" in a larger capital; the text is copied as printed. The last paragraph breaks off mid-sentence at the foot of the page and continues on the next page.
